_about: Sourced reference values for new species in plandscape.fauna (session 3). Fields with a url carry a verbatim quote from the fetched page; fields marked design=true are our choices where no source was found, with the reason. Metres and m/s converted from the source's units.

shoulder.quote: The raccoon stands 9 to 10 inches at the shoulder and weighs 6 to 12 lbs.

length.quote: Body length ranges from 603 to 950 mm. Their tails comprise about 42% to 52% of their length, from 192 to 405 mm.

mass.quote: generally weigh from six to seven kilograms. Weight varies with habitat and region, though, and can range from 1.8 to 10.4kg.

run.quote: Their common gait is a shuffle like walk, however, they are able to reach speeds of 15 miles per hour on the ground.

walk.why: no sourced walking speed; GPS hourly displacement 0.18–0.35 km/h (Hill et al. 2023, PMC10300129) is a lower bound

active.quote: Raccoons are nocturnal and seldom active in the daytime.

group.quote: Primarily a solitary animal, the only real social groups raccoons form are that of mother and young.

habitat.quote: they in fact locate and capture food by dabbling at the water's edge.

length.quote: Terrapene c. carolina is about 15 cm x 10 cm in size
length.note: Virginia means 132.4 (m) and 130.1 mm (f) CL (virginiaherpetologicalsociety.com); T. c. major ~18 cm

run.quote: reaching a maximum velocity of 0.49 m/sec at 31.9°C

walk.quote: Turtle speeds in the field averaged 0.05 m/s
walk.note: proxy: ornate box turtle (T. ornata); daily travel ~32–50 m (Carnegie MNH; Smithsonian)

active.quote: In the summer, they are most active early in the morning or after it rains.

group.quote: The turtles are often found together and show no agression towards each other.

height.note: ADW gives ~60 cm standing, an outlier against 0.97–1.37 m length

length.quote: They stand approximately 60 cm tall and are 97 to 137 cm long.

steps.quote: Typical Walking rates in water are 20-30 steps per minute but can be faster in very shallow water or on land.

walk.why: 25 steps/min (Kushlan) × 0.35 m step (design: no sourced step length)

flight.quote: Typical flight speed for herons (not during migration) = average is 24 mph, but ranges from 9-60 mph
flight.note: the simulation walks it away instead; run = 3 m/s is a design value

run.why: ground escape stand-in; real herons flush by flying (~10.7 m/s)

hip.why: no sourced hip height; about half the standing height

active.quote: most of their activity occurs around dawn and dusk.

group.quote: Though great blue herons hunt alone, they typically nest in colonies.

habitat.quote: the Great Blue Heron is found along lakeshores, rivers, ponds, streams, and occasionally grassy fields near water.
